source: I'll be swift. I know you're a busy woman.
Ophelia recommended I speak with you. I understand there's reason to believe you may have exhibited—or witnessed—suspicious behavior as of late.
What have you to say on this subject?
Is this about that 'spy' rumor? I am innocent! I am good! I never leave the castle—
Yes, that's it. I haven't left Elsinore in weeks!
And what of any letters you might be passing? Notes of a sort?
Do my men have your willing permission to search your room for such letters?
Search away! I cannot read or write. Do I look like a learned woman to you?
Ah... interesting. So you have no means of communication.
Think upon it, Bernardo. Who wishes to see the King and my lady brought to their knees?
Who hates them more than anything? Who crows his displeasure with them day and night, as far and as wide as he possibly can?
...You're implying Hamlet is the spy?
Of course! That boy is dangerous and unpredictable. It is him you ought to interrogate.
That's all for now, Irma. You may go.
Hrmf. A waste of my day and my words...
Irma. How can I assist?
Lady Ophelia told me to come down here and speak with you! What is it you desire?
Apologies. Lady Ophelia must have been mistaken. I've no need to speak with you.
(Ah, right, the morning meeting hasn't occurred yet... He hasn't delivered news about the spy. I'm too soon.)
Now, Lord Hamlet... I'm certain this is just a formality.
You can drop that, you know.
The 'Lord.' I never liked it from you and I don't like it now.
But then you always were more inclined to formalities than Laertes or me, I suppose.
Let's keep things on task, Hamlet.
Your summoning here indicates that you have been, ah, the subject of some suspicion.
What a surprise! My uncle suspects me a spy?
Of course not—because I would never suspect such a thing. I've known you all my life. Don't you think I'd know if you were?
You coming to see me is timely. Your uncle, ah, asked me to speak with you about the information leaks we've experienced lately.
Listen. I had dismissed my uncle's concerns as paranoia, but they may be founded.
My lord Hamlet? What are you doing here?
Ophelia told me to come find you.
She did? What for?
You mean you don't know? Well, then, it's of no consequence.
Although, while I'm here, there is one matter worth discussing...
I've found a set of odd notes in the gallery.
The... gallery? Where, my lord?
The notes were tucked away in one of the bookshelves near the door.
I thought nothing of them before, but now, I'm not so sure.
They're very odd. I... had thought someone left them in the gallery by mistake. So I left them.
Fascinating. When I've a spare moment, I'll have a look in the gallery.
But Hamlet, more to the point... your mental state lately. Your ramblings, your wanderings. Are you...
Is there anything I can do?
No. No, there isn't.
All I need is to be left in peace.
You can trust me, Hamlet. I hope you know that.
I should go. Farewell for now.
Guard Captain. Why did Ophelia ask me to come here?
My lady, I hate to trouble you, but someone has recommended you visit me for an interrogation.
Ophelia did?
It bears investigation, however trivial it may seem.
Ah. I see. She thinks I'm this horrible 'spy' my husband's so concerned about.
Tell me, good captain. Do you believe I'm capable of sabotaging my husband?
...No, my lady. I don't.
Have you any proof to reinforce this interrogation?
I'm embarrassed, my lady. My profound apologies.
Hmph. I thought not. I'll take my leave of you now. This is an incredible insult. I don't know what to say.
To you, Ophelia, or anyone else.
Yes. She mentioned you'd want to speak to me.
I can't imagine what about. Apologies, my lady.
(Ah, right. He hasn't delivered news to the court about his suspicions yet. I'm too early.)
My lady, I hate to trouble you, but I've been informed of some troublesome news.
It bears investigation, however unbelievable it may be.
What do you mean? My husband's investigating me? Whatever for?
He's concerned about some recent behavior of yours. I'll stop short of naming any further accusations aloud.
So someone must have seen me going through his things. Is that it?
I see. Ophelia saw my rummaging and came right to you about it. Is that it?
So... you admit to it?
I do. But not for the reasons you might think.
Bernardo, can you keep a secret?
I... it depends, my lady, on what that secret might be...
My late husband gave me a very special gift. I think my darling Claudius is hiding it from me.
A certain amulet of mine. It was... near and dear to me, and incredibly special.
Hamlet wore it into battle. It was a present for him. It came with me when I arrived from my father's lands, as a girl.
He wore it when we were wed. And when he was to be buried... I draped it round his neck. But then... at the funeral... it was gone.
I know for certain Claudius took it. And I thought perhaps I could find it. But I'm sure he's absconded with it.
Dropped it into the ocean, melted it down. Buried it deep and far away, as he does with all things painful.
And I don't think I shall ever find it again.
I had no idea.
My lady, I apologize for the intrusion.
This is a hole I must fill alone. Thank you for your understanding, Bernardo.
How terrible.
What's all this, now? You summoned, good Captain?
Are we in trouble? If so, I didn't do it!
My ladies, I'm afraid you are, in fact, in trouble.
Someone spotted you acting strangely in various places around the castle, and it's my duty to investigate.
Can you offer any elaboration as to what you were doing?
Oh, of course! You see, we were in deep trouble, and—Ow!
(Quiet, Guilda. If we tell him the truth, it'll just make us look like idiots.)
(Do you want your father to know about our dilemma? Because I don't.)
Nothing, Captain.
You have no excuse for your behavior? Are you aware that failing to comply with this investigation is tantamount to treason?
Very well, then. Perhaps some time in a cell will loosen your tongues.
What? Surely you can't mean—
Oh, I do.
As of yet, I've no reason to suspect you. Although now that I have you here, I might as well ask.
What do you know of any attempts to spy on the residents of this castle?
I have some rather troubling news to announce at this morning's court pertaining to some possible treason occurring under our noses.
It is eerily opportune you came to visit me.
W-Well, nothing in particular!
We only came here to eat!
And meet with the King, of course.
He summoned us. Said he wanted to meet with us. I imagine it has to do with the prince?
But we haven't met him yet! We'd hardly arrived, and whoosh! Ophelia appeared out of nowhere and sent us to talk to you.
And to watch over Hamlet, of course.
Watch over... Hamlet?
The King has asked us to keep an eye on Hamlet's comings and goings. He's concerned about his nephew's health.
I see. That does make a good deal of sense.
Do you feel you've been successful in your efforts?
Well, er...
We haven't even met him yet! We'd hardly arrived, and whoosh! Ophelia appeared out of nowhere and sent us to talk to you.
The man's not the same as we remember!
Something does seem to be weighing on his conscience terribly. Perhaps you ought to give him a visit. Or he a visit to you.
You may go. Apologies for the distraction.
No concern, Bernardo. We'll take our leave of you.
Some time in the cells will straighten them out.
Stay out of trouble, ladies.
No promises!
Ah, the good poet. Surprising to see you here.
Ophelia asked me to speak with you. It was only a matter of time, I suppose. I'm a troublemaker at heart.
Well, perhaps a troublemaker knows how to curb others' troublemaking.
What do you know of any threats to the state?
Me? Why, nothing. Although, come to think of it...
From the guard quarters' window, I've seen multiple people leaving the castle in the wee hours of the morning.
Sometimes they seem to head to town, other times to the docks.
Of course, one might reason they'd woken up in the night with a sudden powerful thirst for a mug of wine, but-- it seems unlikely.
More like they're up to something they'd rather not be caught doing.
Ahem. Fascinating. Late at night, you said?
I'll have Marcellus investigate further as soon as I'm, er, able to do so.
You don't know?
I can't think of anything immediate, no.
Well, then! I'll get out of the hot seat and be on my merry way.
(Right. Bernardo hasn't addressed the spy publicly yet—and won't for a couple hours. I'm a bit too early.)
My lady Brit, I'll be brief.
I already know, Captain. You're going to ask me about this spy business, aren't you?
Well, I know who your so-called 'spy' is. It's the Queen.
M-my lady, that's a rather serious accusation. Don't you think?
Not at all, for she's no spy. I saw her rummaging through the King's rooms myself. She's the one who's given him such cause to fear.
Merely a wife looking for something lost in her husband's items... every evening, just before midnight. Perfectly reasonable behavior!
If her intentions are pure, then it would seem he has no spy to fear. Isn't that true?
Yet we have proof that someone has been passing letters to Fortinbras. This spy reaches beyond the King's disturbed belongings.
I see. Then you're looking for someone who hates King Claudius enough to want him deposed.
Were I you, I'd be looking at the surly, unstable teen right under my nose.
Obviously! He's got an axe to grind and a throne to reclaim.
Er, fascinating theory. At any rate, you're free to go. Thank you for your time, my lady Brit.
Anytime, good Captain. By which I mean: Don't do this to me again. I'm a very busy girl.
So? What did you need me for? Ophelia failed to explain anything crucial.
Need you for? Why, nothing, my lady.
Ugh! She was just wasting my time. How like her. I'll be going now.
(Right. That meeting hasn't happened yet... no one knows about the spy.)
My good lord Polonius. A pleasure, as always.
How can I help, my lad?
Is this about the King's troubling suspicions?
Indeed. You know as well as I how rattled he's been lately.
